newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan cancels December leaded reformate tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan cancels December leaded reformate tender.

text.p: High international gasoline prices and falling domestic demand has prompted Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) to cancel its requirement for leaded reformate in December, an official said on Thursday.
CPC had tendered to buy a 250,000 barrel-cargo of 95-octane leaded reformate for December 1-15 delivery to Keelung or Taichung in a tender which closed October 16 and was valid for two days.
In the same tender, CPC also sought two 250,000 barrel- cargoes of unleaded reformate for November 21-30 and December 1-15 delivery.
The official said CPC awarded the unleaded tender to two different sellers.
It bought the November cargo at $25.90 per barrel on a cost-and-freight basis and the December cargo at a slightly lower price, the official said.
"Even at $25.90, the price is higher than expected," the official said.
In its last tender, CPC paid $23.80 per barrel for an unleaded cargo for November 1-20 delivery.
But CPC were not prepared to pay current high levels for its leaded requirement, the official said.
"Local demand for leaded gasoline is getting smaller," the official said. "We want to reconsider the tender. If prices come off, we will reconsider re-issuing it."
